{{Short description|Norwegian biochemist}}
'''Helge Larsen''' (25 April 1922 – 11 March 2005) was a Norwegian biochemist and microbiologist.

He was born in [[Ålesund]] as a son of a merchant. He [[examen artium|finished]] his secondary education in 1940 before graduating with the [[sivilingeniør|siv.ing.]] degree from the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] in 1944. After graduating, he was employed by the same institution as a [[research assistant]]. Having spent the years 1947 to 1950 in the United States, Larsen took the [[Doctor of Technology|dr.techn.]] degree in 1954. He was appointed as a professor of technical biochemistry at the Norwegian Institute of Technology in 1955, retiring in 1992.<ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Helge Larsen|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|url=http://www.snl.no/Helge_Larsen|language=no|accessdate=2 September 2026}}</ref><ref name=nbl>{{cite encyclopedia|year=|title=Helge Larsen|encyclopedia=[[Norsk biografisk leksikon]]|first=Kjell|last=Eimhjellen|editor=[[Knut Helle|Helle, Knut]]|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=https://nbl.snl.no/Helge_Larsen|language=no|accessdate=8 September 2026}}</ref> 

As biochemistry was a relatively new subject at the time, Larsen was instrumental in shaping the education at the Norwegian Institute of Technology. With his research having impact in the industry, particularly the [[fishing industry]], he also chaired the committee that planned the 1972 establishment of the [[Norwegian College of Fishery Science]].<ref name=nbl/>

He was inducted into Trondheim's [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]] and [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]], both in 1955,<ref name=nbl/> followed by the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] in 1967.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|title=Norske medlemmer|publisher=Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|access-date=2 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715142138/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26857|archive-date=15 July 2007}}</ref> He received an [[honorary degree]] from the [[University of Gothenburg]] in 1990, and honorary membership of the [[Norwegian Biochemical Society]] in 1991. He died in March 2005 in Trondheim, aged 82.<ref name=nbl/>
